tools.name: start_task
tools.description: Opens a work record for one legal task and returns the clarifying questions the framework needs answered (step 1, define the task), less any already answered in `answers`. The first two are the country and, in Australia, the state or territory: ask them first. Read the skill ailf://skills/ai-law-fra

tools.name: record_answers
tools.description: Adds the user’s answers to the clarifying questions to the work record. Returns the questions still open, or, once all are answered, the research the task requires.

tools.name: record_research
tools.description: Adds research findings, each with its source, quote and confirmation status, to the work record. Returns the required research still missing, or the scoring anchors and the governance ceiling the evidence sets.

tools.name: assess_and_decide
tools.description: Scores the AI option on adoption, efficiency and governance (step 2), caps governance by the recorded evidence, scores the manual route, and returns the decision, its reasons and the order of preference.

tools.name: plan_human_work
tools.description: Sets the level of each of the seven stages of the task (step 3) from the recorded answers, research and decision, and returns what the lawyer and the AI may and may not do at each stage.

tools.name: work_record
tools.description: Returns the work record as markdown (steps 4 and 5): the task, the evidence, the decision, the plan, what the AI did, and the checks, approval and release left for the lawyer.

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: Searches the framework’s published practice areas, tasks, jurisdiction versions, jurisdictions, firm-wide obligations and software profiles. Returns titles, ids and ailawframework.com links.

tools.name: get_task_guidance
tools.description: Returns one task from the practice library: how AI may be used, its level, what the lawyer must review, its checkpoints, restrictions and sources, and its jurisdiction versions.

tools.name: get_jurisdiction_guidance
tools.description: Returns the framework’s notes for one jurisdiction, and which stored AI instruments apply to a task in a court or tribunal. Name the forum, or court "no" when no court is involved. A gap means no instrument is stored for that forum.

tools.name: get_software_profile
tools.description: Returns the framework’s research on one AI product and plan: its facts, the governance considerations found, and the cited sources with their review dates. Accepts a profile id or a product name.

tools.name: search_precedents
tools.description: Searches the published precedent library (letters, agreements, clauses, checklists, forms, policies and more for every practice area) by title, summary and when to use it. Returns ids, titles, kinds, practice area ids, jurisdictions and the date each states the law as at. The full text is available

tools.name: get_precedent
tools.description: Returns one published precedent’s details: summary, when to use it, authorities, the AI-use guidance (level, what AI may and must not do, what the lawyer checks), licence, the date it states the law as at and how the library maintains it. The text itself is available through the signed-in firm conne

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: For a new user, or when asked what this is: what the AI Law Framework decides, the first questions it asks (country, then state or territory), the five steps, the skills and starting prompts, and a fictional sample matter the user can run to see a finished work record.

tools.name: get_framework
tools.description: Returns the AI Law Framework’s rules: the five steps, the three pillars and their anchors, the decision rule, the four levels, the seven stages and their matrix, and the rules that admit no exception.
